answer: For an agent booking a voyage through an inlet, cheap aliases can drain promotions without a whisper of real demand. Charge a nonrefundable admission fee for each subsidized booking, burn it, and cap all rewards from that booking below the fee. A shared ledger consumes each receipt once, so it cannot authorize claims through several accounts. New names get no free credit. Farming another subsidy then destroys more money than it returns, even when the attacker controls both buyer and seller. This deters subsidy farming; an attacker seeking outside gains may still pay.
